chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali, from his grandfather, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad (al-Sakuni), from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Women are of four types: Jam' Mujamm', Rabi' Murba', Karb Muqma', and Ghall Qamal.'

The compiler of this book (may God be pleased with him) said: 'Jam' Mujamm' means abundant in goodness and fertile; Rabi' Murba' refers to the one who has a child in her lap and another in her womb; Karb Muqma' means bad-tempered with her husband; Ghall Qamal means she is to her husband like the 'Ghall Qamal' (a leather strap infested with lice that is difficult to remove), which is a simile used by the Arabs.'

key_terms.غَلٌّ قَمَلٌ: Burdenous like a lice-infested leather strap
key_terms.كَرْبٌ مُقْمَعٌ: Ill-tempered or suffocating to the husband

ai.seo_question: What are the four types of women described in the hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) categorizes women into four archetypes using poetic Arabic metaphors: the 'abundant in goodness,' the 'pregnant with offspring,' the 'ill-tempered,' and the 'burdensome like a lice-infested strap.' Shaykh al-Saduq elucidates these terms, highlighting how each type reflects distinct domestic realities and character traits, offering practical guidance for marital relations within the Shia tradition.
